data.name: Anteros
data.long_meaning: Anteros is a Greek god of requited love and self-sacrificing passion. He is also known as the god of unrequited love and the protector of friendships.

in_hebrew.name: אנטרוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אנטרוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אנτερος' (Anteros), שפירושה 'אהבה הדדית' או 'אהבת גומלין'. במילון של שמות הנוצרים, אנטרוס מתאר את האהבה והחיבה שמבטאים יחסים הדדיים בין שני אנשים. השם משקף ערכים של חברות, יחסים הדדיים ואהבה.

in_greek.name: Άντερος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Άντερος (Anteros) στην ελληνική παράδοση, συμβολίζει την αμοιβαία αγάπη και την ανταπόκριση στην αγάπη. Ο όρος προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'αντερος', που σημαίνει 'αμοιβαία αγάπη' ή 'αγάπη που ανταποκρίνεται'. Στην πνευματική και πολιτιστική παράδοση της Ελλάδας και της Χριστιανικής Ορθοδοξίας, το όνομα Αντερος φέρει τη σημασία της αμοιβαίας αγάπης και της βαθιάς ψυχικής σύνδεσης.

in_latin.name: Anteros
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Anteros in traditione Christiana, mutuam amoris reciprocationem designat. Etymologia nominis a voce Graeca 'Anteros' derivatur, quae amorem mutuum et reciprocum significat. In usu ecclesiastico et spirituali, Anteros exprimit necessitudinem amoris et caritatis inter duas personas, quae in vicissitudine et consensu fundatur.

in_english.name: Anteros
in_english.long_meaning: The name Anteros originates from the Greek word 'Αντερος' (Anteros), meaning 'mutual love' or 'reciprocal affection'. In Christian tradition, Anteros symbolizes the love and affection that characterize reciprocal relationships between two individuals. The name reflects values of friendship, mutual respect, and loving interchange. Historically, Anteros has been associated with the concept of requited love and spiritual bonding.

data.cultural_impact: Anteros is a character in various Greek myths, frequently depicted as a young man with wings who holds a pair of roses in his hands, symbolizing love and sacrifice.
data.spiritual_significance: Anteros represents the desire to give love selflessly, without the expectation of receiving it in return, themes which are present in Christian teachings about love and service to others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Anteros was a god of requited love in ancient Greek religion. The name Anteros carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Anteros was a god of requited love, meaning love that is returned or reciprocated. He was often depicted as a beautiful youth with a pair of wings on his shoulders, and was said to be the brother of Eros, the god of love.

In Christianity, this name symbolizes the unconditional and sacrificial love of God towards humanity. It is a reminder of God's endless compassion and the call for believers to embody this love in their own lives.
